11.4.1Step One. Freeze the Current State ​

In briefFreezing is a dated snapshot of the analytical starting point, preserving what was known, unknown, and which model version was used. It does not require the world to stop changing.

Record the evidence cutoff, objects, variables, unknowns, disputes, and model version. Information obtained after the cutoff must not be fed back into the starting point. If it needs to be used, create a new version of the run.

11.4.1Note

Understanding this section

11.4.1 Step one: freeze the current state

Freezing is a dated snapshot of the analytical starting point, preserving what was known, unknown, and which model version was used. It does not require the world to stop changing.

Evidence cutoff means “the latest acquisition time of material allowed in this run,” not that all described events occurred then. A record of yesterday's event received today becomes knowledge usable only today; event, acquisition, and model-entry clocks remain separate under 11.3.2.

A snapshot specifies at least objects, task, variables, values and their status, unknowns, disputes, sources, and model version. Equal values may differ in status: measured inventory 6 and inventory stipulated as 6 for projection are not the same evidence. Disputes are not blanks that must vanish; two compatible states may remain.

Freezing the model includes actual rules and key parameters, not just a filename. If a queue originally assumes 3 processed per hour and later 1, specify whether knowledge, actual capacity, or only a new scenario changed. Otherwise a seemingly continuous curve may splice different models.

Late evidence can of course be used, but in a new run version. The old version evaluates judgments under information then available; the new version serves the current task. Both may coexist. Reconstructing an accident from later evidence is retrospective explanation, not a relabeled preaccident prediction.

Freezing enables comparison, not guaranteed starting accuracy. If material is wrong, append corrections and recompute dependencies; “already frozen” cannot justify refusing correction, nor may the corrected starting point replace old records to erase the original error.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify task, object, and evidence cutoff, preserving actual acquisition times item by item.

  2. 2

    Register variable and unknown status, sources, and disputes without zero-filling missing values.

  3. 3

    Freeze rules, parameters, and versions so derivational responsibility for the same inputs is traceable.

  4. 4

    Create a new run for later material while keeping the old one traceable; corrections propagate along dependencies.

Distinctions to keep clear

Freeze a knowledge snapshot

Bounds the information used in this projection.

≠

Freeze the world

Reality may continue changing.

Prediction made at the time

Uses only pre-cutoff material.

≠

Retrospective reconstruction

May use later evidence, but must be relabeled accordingly.

Unknown

Insufficient material to assign a value.

≠

Zero or did not occur

Needs corresponding observation; it does not come from a blank.

Teaching construction: a late fault noticeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsFault time, capacity change, and notice credibility are fictional assumptions; no real machine is involved.

At 08:00 freeze V1: 6 pending repairs, arrivals 2/hour, processing 3/hour. Under B_next_hour=max(0,B+arrivals−processing), 09:00 projects to 5. At 08:30 a credible notice reports that the machine slowed to 1/hour at 07:50. Create V2 and recalculate 08:00–09:00 as 7. V1 derives from material available then; V2 is a retrospective correction incorporating late information, not proof that 7 was predicted at 08:00.

BoundaryV2 does not mean the machine slowed again at 08:30; do not count the event twice.

Apollo 13: a fault not yet understood at the timeDocumented case

When the 1970 Apollo 13 accident first occurred, its cause and severity were unknown. The report then describes ground personnel progressively checking electrical and oxygen readings. This section focuses on the temporal development of knowledge: retrospective findings cannot be inserted into the first alarm moment.

SourceNASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15Chapter 4 Part 5, printed pp.4-44,4-46; PDF pp.153,155, Understanding the ProblemReading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsSupports only incomplete initial understanding and subsequent checking. This lesson has no complete second-by-second information sets and did not reconstruct prediction accuracy at the time.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleSince the fault is later known to have occurred at 07:50, it can be inserted into material known at 08:00.

What it limitsEarlier occurrence does not mean earlier knowledge; preserve knowledge timing.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Complete snapshot fields do not imply error-free observations.
  • Later discovery of wrong old inputs does not prevent a corrected version despite freezing.
  • Do not replace old predictions with hindsight evidence to inflate accuracy.

Scope and open questions

The original investigation explicitly distinguishes initial confusion from subsequent judgment, illustrating why evidence timing must be frozen.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Why must V1 and V2 both be retained?

  2. 2

    If inventory 6 proves a recording error after freezing, may it no longer be corrected?

Why must V1 and V2 both be retained?

V1 answers how judgment was made then; V2 answers how new material revises it. Deleting V1 destroys grounds for evaluation and correction.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If inventory 6 proves a recording error after freezing, may it no longer be corrected?

Append a correction and create a new version, without overwriting the old run or treating the correction as a new inventory arrival.

11.4.2Step Two. Identify Actors and Circles ​

In briefA shared roster, label, or one collaboration need not form a circle with stable boundaries; one choice need not reveal fixed personality. First establish whom we discuss and how they connect.

Use Parts 9 and 10. If a circle has no grounds for object facts and the grouping gain claimed for it is not supported, retain it as a candidate grouping. If there is insufficient support for a personality hypothesis, retain it as a variable candidate. Do not turn candidates into entities merely to complete the graph.

11.4.2Note

Understanding this section

11.4.2 Step two: identify actors and circles

A shared roster, label, or one collaboration need not form a circle with stable boundaries; one choice need not reveal fixed personality. First establish whom we discuss and how they connect.

Part Nine brings actors' slow, mid, and fast states and conditional action sets into analysis. Part Ten examines establishing circle-object facts from documents, relationships, and interactions, separately testing grouping gain for the task. This section uses those results, not permanent personality types assigned to everyone.

Actors may be individuals actually having effects or supported collective objects. Before graph inclusion, state evidence for task-relevant responsibilities, capabilities, resources, and relations. A name's appearance or shared job title does not automatically establish decision-making authority for the same action; inferring psychological motives from office also exceeds the boundary.

Candidate circle groupings remain analytically useful for proposing connections, shared resources, and boundaries to check. But a candidate cannot first become an established collective node whose assumed will explains member behavior; that makes object and mechanism circularly certify each other.

Retaining variable candidates when personality evidence is insufficient means “this difference may matter and remains to be distinguished,” not permission to collect more private experiences. Prioritize task-required observable behavior and conditions such as schedules, authorization, and equipment availability; do not misattribute equipment constraints to poor responsibility.

Circle boundaries may be nested, overlapping, or parallel by dimension. Maintenance and purchasing teams sharing a coordinator does not mean they merged into one object; examine people, budgets, permission, and task chains separately. Documents, membership, sustained interaction, or shared exposure can also support corresponding object facts without unified will in every circle. Only grouping-related explanatory or foresight gain claims separately require G1; untested G1 cannot erase independent object facts. When scale changes, reconfirm meanings of nodes and edges.

This step keeps two material accounts: facts about agents' and circles' identities, membership, and relationships; and gains from using those groupings in the current projection task. Reliable documents and interaction records may support the former; only formal support for the latter checks G1. When both are missing, retain candidates, but do not misstate absence of G1 as absence of these people in reality.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    List agents relevant to the current outcome and their checkable roles and conditions.

  2. 2

    Check candidate circles' connections, boundaries, recurring mechanisms, and resources; do not reify them directly from names.

  3. 3

    Separate supported states from candidate personality or collective variables.

  4. 4

    Retain candidate status for unestablished groupings rather than letting them carry established causation.

Distinctions to keep clear

Task role

Responsibilities, capabilities, and authority supported by materials.

≠

Personality essence

Cannot be presumed from one instance of role performance.

Candidate grouping

An analytical division whose common mechanism awaits checking.

≠

Supported circle object

Requires corresponding object boundaries and operating materials.

Membership overlap

The same person participates in two groups.

≠

The two circles are identical

Additionally requires identity grounds for the declared dimension.

Teaching construction: one person across groups is not unified capacityTeaching scenario

AssumptionsRoles and authority are wholly stipulated in the construction; no actual person's capabilities or psychology are judged.

Fictional repair team Alpha has technicians A and B; procurement team Beta has purchaser C and coordinator B. A is qualified to repair, C has procurement authority, and B only transmits paperwork. Roster overlap supports only overlap in personnel; C cannot be counted as repair capacity, nor B regarded as authorized to approve purchases. If all that is known is that the three share a chat group, even these groupings remain to be checked.

BoundaryCommunication in one group may supply an information channel but does not directly establish shared budgets, unified will, or action permission.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleBecause B belongs to both groups, they can be merged into one agent with unlimited complementarity.

What it limitsShared membership does not remove skill, authority, time, or resource constraints.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Useful grouping is not established entity status; provisional nonreification also does not mean members are unconnected.
  • Do not fill default motives when psychological materials are absent or treat an individual's weaknesses as the entire system's bottleneck.
  • Actual collection remains constrained by purpose, necessity, and authority.

Scope and open questions

This unit explains object admission and candidate status; materials sufficient to establish a particular actual team under the book's complete circle contract have not been obtained. Apollo role rosters cannot masquerade as completed circle identification; an explicit construction shows nonentailment.

  • Actual team boundaries, resource allocation, recurring connections, and authorization records were not provided; stable circle-object status is not granted here.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Can a group be recognized as a stable circle from a membership roster alone?

  2. 2

    If repairs slow down, may ‘employees lack responsibility’ be assigned first?

Can a group be recognized as a stable circle from a membership roster alone?

No. The roster may provide candidate entry, but task-relevant connections, boundaries, and operating materials are still required.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If repairs slow down, may ‘employees lack responsibility’ be assigned first?

No. First check distinguishable conditions such as equipment, part arrival, qualifications, and scheduling; personality inferences require independent support.

11.4.3Step Three. Separate Conditions in the Two Channels ​

In briefMaterial feasibility and how people understand, experience, or accept something are two kinds of conditions. When one kind of material is missing, pause inferences depending on it without necessarily stopping every other independent judgment.

List the relevant material conditions separately for the task. Also list the relevant experience–meaning conditions and declare the bridges needed between channels. If missing information from the other channel affects the current judgment, retain the unknown. Do not fill the gap by assuming symmetry. A channel genuinely irrelevant to the current task may be marked not applicable with a reason. Do not collect experiential material for the sake of completing the form. Suspend only propagation that depends on the missing channel. Independently established states and paths can still be carried forward.

11.4.3Note

Understanding this section

11.4.3 Step three: separate dual-channel conditions

Material feasibility and how people understand, experience, or accept something are two kinds of conditions. When one kind of material is missing, pause inferences depending on it without necessarily stopping every other independent judgment.

M records task-relevant material conditions such as quantities, equipment, work hours, interfaces, and budgets; Ψ records experience–meaning conditions such as expressed feelings, interpretations of meaning, or understandings of justification. These are neither mutually exclusive worlds nor default mirror images, and evidence for one does not automatically establish the other.

A cross-channel bridge explains which material change affects which experience–meaning variable through what distinguishable mechanism, or conversely how it produces action and material consequences. Restored repair equipment does not mean restored employee trust; a survey expressing support does not mean actual increased processing capacity. Connection requires a corresponding bridge and temporal materials.

Missing and not applicable differ. If the question asks only the number of items a specified machine can complete under fixed settings, personal experience may be inapplicable to that local calculation, with reasons stated. If the question asks willingness to work overtime, experience, meaning, and autonomous choice may alter the answer; missingness cannot be filled as willingness through an assumption of symmetry.

A local pause protects evidential boundaries. Unknown willingness to work overtime does not prevent reporting checked machine capacity, but it blocks continued inference along ‘the machine has spare capacity → employees will stay → the backlog must clear’. Separate the supported capacity path from the behavioral path awaiting checking, preventing both spread of unknowns throughout the system and bypassing of unknowns.

Do not collect experiential materials for formal completeness. Questions about psychology, health, or private life require actual necessity and appropriate boundaries; marking task-irrelevant Ψ fields not applicable is more honest than filling guesses or creating intrusive surveys.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Fix the question first, then list task-relevant M and Ψ variables item by item.

  2. 2

    For cross-channel inferences, state the bridge, direction, time, and material responsibilities.

  3. 3

    Mark missing relevant fields unknown; give reasons for inapplicability of irrelevant fields.

  4. 4

    Pause only paths actually dependent on missing fields, preserving independently established results.

Distinctions to keep clear

Material capability

The scope equipment and resources can support under given conditions.

≠

Willingness or identification

Concerns agents' experience, interpretation, and choice, requiring separate materials.

Unknown

Relevant but sufficient materials have not yet been obtained.

≠

Not applicable

Does not affect the declared local question, with reasons given.

Local pause

Stops inferences dependent on a missing bridge.

≠

Complete shutdown of work

Analysis unaffected by the gap may continue.

Teaching construction: one result known, another unknownTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEquipment capacity and hours are constructed; the capacity ceiling guarantees neither actual demand, behavior, nor authorization.

A fictional device has two idle hours, processes at most 3 items per hour, and has sufficient materials. Its equipment ceiling is therefore 6 items. Actual completion also requires a qualified person present; all that is known is that their shift has ended, not whether they are willing and authorized to work overtime. The equipment-capacity ceiling of 6 may be given, but not guaranteed actual completion of 6. Unknown willingness and unknown permission also cannot replace each other.

BoundaryIf the question only calculates the device's theoretical ceiling, experience need not be collected; if it asks actual completion, corresponding behavioral and authority conditions are required.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleWe do not know whether employees are willing to work overtime, so even hourly machine capacity cannot be reported.

What it limitsMissingness blocks only the actual-completion path dependent on willingness, without erasing independent equipment conditions.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleThe machine is back to normal, so everyone must trust management again.

What it limitsThe bridge from material conditions to meaning is missing; it cannot be filled symmetrically.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • The M/Ψ distinction serves the task and does not require equally long columns for every object.
  • Self-reported meaning has its own evidential status and cannot be replaced directly by machine data.
  • If behavioral feedback changes capacity, an earlier ‘not applicable’ judgment should be rechecked.

Scope and open questions

This examines the formal boundary against automatic entailment between the two channels. The spaceflight reports read here do not supply sufficient individual-experience materials; successful rescue is not used to infer trust or motivation backward.

  • Actual overtime choices and experiential materials were not obtained; unknown fields are not filled, and no personnel survey is conducted.

  2. 2

    When may Ψ be marked not applicable?

If a machine can process 6 items in two hours, why is the actual completed quantity still unknown?

Actual execution conditions such as presence, qualifications, willingness, and authorization remain unmet or unchecked.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

When may Ψ be marked not applicable?

Strictly limit the question to local capability unaffected by the variable and explain why; recheck if the question expands.

11.4.4Step Four. Declare Clocks, Thresholds, Capacity, and Delay ​

In brief‘It will get through’ is insufficient: ask how long it takes, how much can pass at once, what is lost en route, and whether the window has already been missed. An arrow without a clock easily turns possible into timely and available stock into adequate supply.

Identify each variable’s update clock. If a channel has capacity limits, delay, loss, saturation, reversal, or a recovery window, register them before propagation.

11.4.4Note

Understanding this section

11.4.4 Step four: declare clocks, thresholds, capacities, and delays

‘It will get through’ is insufficient: ask how long it takes, how much can pass at once, what is lost en route, and whether the window has already been missed. An arrow without a clock easily turns possible into timely and available stock into adequate supply.

Variable-update clocks may use fixed intervals, event triggers, batch settlement, or slow, intermediate, and fast cycles at different levels. Inventory checked hourly, instantaneous alarms, and work hours recorded only the next day cannot be treated as simultaneous states without alignment. Observation frequency also differs from actual change frequency.

Thresholds need triggering direction and equality conventions; capacities need units and windows; delays must distinguish execution, transmission, and recording. Register losses, saturation, reversals, and recovery windows only when relevant and supported by materials. Unsupported details remain unknown rather than assuming identical nonlinearities in every system.

A capacity of 3 items per hour does not mean 3 items can be completed immediately; total stock of 10 also does not mean 10 can be obtained at a particular location within 10 minutes. If a channel waits an hour before transport, a recovery action may arrive too late for the current task window. Temporal constraints can change option rankings without changing the eventual total.

Near thresholds, distinguish measurement error and hysteresis: crossing an alarm value may differ from actual harm, and if cooling is still needed after a rise before recovery, recrossing a threshold in reverse cannot instantly erase downtime. These are recording responsibilities, not a claim that every object exhibits hysteresis.

Declaring parameters is not accurately estimating them. Sources may be equipment specifications, current observations, or model assumptions, whose statuses should be separated. High-consequence settings require conservatively retained uncertainty ranges; teaching formulas cannot become real control instructions directly.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    For each variable, state its actual change timescale and observation/model-entry clocks.

  2. 2

    Express thresholds, capacities, and windows in consistent units, specifying equality at boundaries.

  3. 3

    Before propagation, register relevant delays, losses, saturation, and recovery conditions; unknowns do not default to zero.

  4. 4

    Check whether an action's arrival still falls within the task window before comparing consequences.

Distinctions to keep clear

Capacity

The maximum throughput supportable within a specified window.

≠

Inventory

The quantity available at a time point; the two differ in units and roles.

Recovery conditions

Conditions and waiting needed to reenter an available state.

≠

Alarm cleared

A record or threshold status changes, which need not mean capacity has recovered.

Recording clock

When a value is obtained or written.

≠

Object clock

When the real variable changes.

Mathematical construction: late replenishment cannot recover a missed windowTeaching scenario

AssumptionsParts cannot be borrowed in advance, each completed item must already have consumed a part, and both arrival time and the strictly exclusive deadline are construction assumptions.

A fictional repair task requires completing 3 items during 08:00—09:00, each consuming 1 part; stock at 08:00 is 1 part. Replenishment of 2 parts arrives only at 09:00, and the task definition requires completion strictly before 09:00. Even if equipment can process 3 items per hour, parts limit this window to at most 1 item; cumulative parts reaching 3 at 09:00 does not make 3 completed in the earlier window.

BoundaryIf the contract permits completion after arrival at 09:00 or extends the task window, the question must be rewritten; the deadline cannot be silently changed to rescue the conclusion.

Apollo 13: consumption rates determine the available windowDocumented case

The report records emergency power-down of the lunar module reducing electrical-energy demand to about 20% of normal operating values and correspondingly reducing cooling-water use. The added point here is that changing consumption rates can change resource duration; initial inventory alone is insufficient.

SourceNASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15Chapter 5, Finding 45(a)—(c), printed p.5-33, PDF page 206Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis is the report's conclusion for a particular mission, not a universal energy-saving coefficient for other systems; 20% does not mean every consumable fell to exactly 20%.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleThe final resource total is sufficient, so demand can be met at every intermediate moment.

What it limitsInventory and throughput are not temporally aligned; an early gap may be irreversible.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • One fixed step size does not fit every event; subdivide critical windows where needed.
  • Unchecked threshold parameters cannot justify actual safety action.
  • Sufficient cumulative supply may still include a temporary shortage during one segment.

Scope and open questions

The original report explicitly records the relationship between energy-use rate and cooling-water consumption, supporting the distinction between inventory and time-window constraints.

Check your understanding

    What are processing 3 items per hour and currently having 3 spare parts, respectively?

  2. 2

What are processing 3 items per hour and currently having 3 spare parts, respectively?

The former is capacity within a time window, the latter inventory at a time point; they constrain jointly but are not interchangeable.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why must it be stated whether the deadline includes equality?

Whether resources arriving at the boundary time enter the task window changes feasibility.

11.4.5Step Five. Inject an Event or Action ​

In briefFirst ask whether something happened, then who did it, to whom, with what consequences, and with what authority. Unauthorized acts may still actually occur, while things written into plans may never happen at all.

A run may include multiple events and actions ordered by time, with their independent sources retained. First determine whether an action occurred, then record the actor, object, consequences, and authorization status separately. Lack of authorization cannot justify deleting a fact about what actually occurred. Plans, proposals, and simulated actions that have yet to occur retain their conditional status and must not be recorded as executed. If a model initiates or carries out a real-world action, valid authorization must be obtained separately. A recommendation for deliberation requires only that its evidence, normative premises, costs, gaps in authority, and conditions for revising the judgment be stated clearly.

11.4.5Note

Understanding this section

11.4.5 Step five: inject events or actions

First ask whether something happened, then who did it, to whom, with what consequences, and with what authority. Unauthorized acts may still actually occur, while things written into plans may never happen at all.

A run may contain multiple events and actions; real chains need not be deleted to ‘look at one at a time’. Each retains independent sources, times, and identities before being connected through grounded temporal order. When order cannot be determined, retain branches under 11.3.2 rather than substituting the order in which tool messages return for real-world order.

Agent, object, consequences, and authorization status are different fields. Observing a machine shut down does not identify its operator; confirming the operator also does not establish their motives or authority. Leave each missing item unknown rather than deleting the entire fact.

Under 11.3's notation, u is reserved for authorized actions that actually occur; observed or reported actions that occurred without authorization may enter e as events, with authority listed separately. This registers world changes without endorsing behavior; multiple references to the same action still apply its corresponding effect only once.

Plans, recommendations, and simulated actions that have not occurred retain conditional status. For example, ‘if another shift is added’ generates hypothetical consequences only and cannot automatically add staff to the baseline state. Approval also does not mean arrival; execution still requires occurrence evidence.

Forming a recommendation for deliberation and executing for someone are two levels of behavior. Recommendations may be offered after making evidence, value premises, costs, authority gaps, and revision conditions explicit. A model actually initiating real action requires separate valid authorization and corresponding protection checks. ‘This option is best’ cannot become an authorization letter, nor can lack of execution authority justify rejecting every bounded analysis.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Check actual-occurrence evidence for each input, distinguishing plans, reports, observations, and simulations.

  2. 2

    Register agents, objects, consequences, and authority separately; one field cannot supply the others.

  3. 3

    Retain sources and ordering for multiple events, without applying the same event twice.

  4. 4

    Recommendations disclose premises and gaps; execution separately obtains valid authorization.

Distinctions to keep clear

Occurrence

Has corresponding factual evidence.

≠

Authorized

A normative and permission status; neither implies the other.

Approved plan

Permission exists, but execution may not yet have occurred.

≠

Resources actually arrived

Occurrence materials are required before changing the baseline state.

Recommendation for deliberation

State a conditional comparison of options.

≠

Implement an action

Changes reality and requires independent valid authorization.

Teaching construction: unauthorized withdrawal and pending replenishmentTeaching scenario

AssumptionsQuantity removed, occurrence evidence, no other stock movements, and resupply status are construction premises; no actual taking is arranged.

A fictional warehouse starts with 5 items. Reliable records show someone took 2 without permission; another 3-item resupply is approved but has not arrived. Known current stock is 3: do not delete unauthorized removal and retain 5, or add approved supplies prematurely and record 6. If resupply later actually arrives, register it separately; only then does stock become 6 under these assumptions.

BoundaryIf removal is only an unverified report, give the report-conditional value rather than claiming a measured stock of 3.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleThis removal was unauthorized and should not enter the formal model.

What it limitsDeleting an actual change distorts later resource projections; preserve the fact and record its unauthorized status separately.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleI recommended more staff, so queue capacity can be increased directly.

What it limitsRecommendation is not execution; changed capacity needs evidence of corresponding occurrence.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Lack of authorization is not a reason to delete facts, and registering facts grants no permission.
  • Unknown ordering of multiple events must not be forced into one sequence.
  • Do not enter simulated actions in executed-action logs.

Scope and open questions

The core is logical independence of fact and authorization. The Apollo report read does not permit checking authority for every action; successful results are not used to infer complete authorization. Explicit constructions test recording rules instead.

  2. 2

Starting stock is 5, an unauthorized withdrawal takes 2, and approved replenishment of 3 has not arrived. How should current inventory be recorded?

3 under the explicit assumptions; unarrived supplies enter only a conditional branch.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Can recommendations still be offered without authority to execute?

A bounded recommendation for deliberation is possible with grounds, normative premises, costs, authority gaps, and revision conditions; it cannot be implemented without authorization.

11.4.6Step Six. Propagate Along Declared Channels ​

In briefOne place changes and another changes later; this is not yet a causal arrow. Preserve known changes first, then ask segment by segment which channel, which period, and which competing explanations were distinguished.

First record directly confirmable state differences, then analyze return signals, indirect effects, and cross-circle cascades. An identified total effect of an intervention may enter a bounded judgment about the outcome. Unidentified parts of the internal mechanism remain unknown. The total effect must not be used to fill in missing edges of propagation. Explaining specific propagation requires corresponding material about channels and temporal order. Where there is only co-occurrence or correlation, retain common background, selection effects, and other competing explanations. Store state differences derived conditionally from the model separately from those observed in reality.

11.4.6Note

Understanding this section

11.4.6 Step Six: Propagate along Declared Channels

One place changes and another changes later; this is not yet a causal arrow. Preserve known changes first, then ask segment by segment which channel, which period, and which competing explanations were distinguished.

Direct state differences also have evidence status: keep measured differences, record-supported inferences, and conditional model calculations separately. ‘Direct’ does not automatically mean a causal effect identified by randomized experiment; uncontrolled before-and-after differences may include shared background changes.

Feedback requires material on return and subsequent state or rule changes; a message’s arrival is not learning. Indirect effects need valid intermediate transmission, and cross-circle cascades need each boundary and resource interface checked. Crossing one layer does not automatically inherit the preceding layer’s efficacy.

Separate total effects from internal mechanisms. A bounded intervention effect on a final outcome identified by an appropriate design may be retained despite unclear mediators; unknown mediators cannot be filled into a unique chain. Conversely, knowing one feasible mechanism does not automatically determine actual total-effect magnitude.

Correlation and co-occurrence may prompt investigation, but shared shocks, selection into records, and reverse effects may produce similar patterns. Specific propagation requires matching timing, interfaces, and flow evidence and explaining how alternatives are distinguished; absent material, mark candidate edges.

Mathematical propagation depends on explicit functions, parameters, and feasible domains. Even positive average gains on each edge may yield no total gain when windows, subgroup selection, or intermediate states do not match; 11.6 develops these interface issues. This step cannot mechanically multiply arrows as facts.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Confirm the starting point and direct state differences’ status and timing.

  2. 2

    List channel, conditions, scope, sources, and competing explanations for every edge.

  3. 3

    Retain identified total effects separately from unknown internal mechanisms.

  4. 4

    Store model derivations separately as conditional results without upgrading them to actual observations.

Distinctions to keep clear

Before-and-after state difference

Change observed across time.

≠

Causal intervention effect

Requires appropriate identification conditions, not before-and-after comparison alone.

A bounded total effect is identified

Answers a limited question about this intervention’s outcome.

≠

Every mediating edge is identified

Requires additional mechanism material.

Return signal

Information returns to an earlier node.

≠

Feedback change and learning

Also require subsequent state or rule changes and corresponding learning evidence.

Mathematical construction: queue calculation and observation are separateTeaching scenario

AssumptionsArrivals precede processing each hour; capacity stays fixed for two hours, no other flows exist, and both branches share initial value and arrivals.

Fictional B0=6 with 2 arrivals per hour. If a breakdown fixes processing capacity at 1, B1=6+2−1=7 and B2=7+2−1=8. If another branch retains capacity 3, B1=5 and B2=4. This is a conditional difference of 4 items under the specified recurrence. Without an actual breakdown intervention or observations, it cannot be reported as ‘breakdown empirically increased backlog by 4’.

BoundaryIf actual breakdown also changes arrivals or measurement rules, this difference cannot transfer directly.

Apollo 13: an evidenced energy–water-use connectionDocumented case

The report connects reduced Lunar Module power consumption, lower heat production, and reduced cooling-water use. Compared with the consumption-rate window in the preceding subsection, this adds that propagation explanations need specific intermediate links, not simply ‘save electricity → everything improves’.

SourceNASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15Chapter 4, Part 5, Return to Earth, printed p. 4-48, final paragraph on PDF page 156Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThe report supports this specific engineering explanation, not attribution of all psychological, organizational, or safety outcomes to saving power; this guide independently estimates no causal-effect magnitude.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleTwo simulations differ by 4, so an actual breakdown’s causal effect has been measured as 4.

What it limitsA simulation comparison is only a model-conditional difference, lacking actual identification design and observation.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleThe total effect is reliable, but one internal link is unknown, so the total effect must be deleted too.

What it limitsRetain the independently valid bounded result and mark the unknown mechanism separately.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Missing mechanism details should neither erase an independently established total effect nor invite invented edges.
  • Evidence for adjacent edges does not guarantee joint applicability; interfaces and windows must be compatible.
  • Retain competing explanations when shared background cannot be excluded.

Scope and open questions

The original report supplies a specific engineering connection, illustrating the need for concrete channels without replacing a causal experiment this guide did not perform.

Shared background, record selection, and other mechanisms can produce the same sequence; corresponding channels and discriminating material are needed.

Does an identified total effect permit completing the internal mechanism graph?

No. Preserve the bounded total effect while leaving unknown mediators unfilled.

11.4.7Step Seven. Generate Paths at Branch Points ​

In briefBranching is not about writing many stories; it preserves conditional differences that may still change the answer. Distinguish ‘only one can occur’ from ‘they may occur together’, then decide between separate and parallel branches.

Conditions, thresholds, actor choices, external disturbances, or uncertainty about mechanisms can all produce branching. Keep mutually exclusive paths separate. Retain parallel paths if they can occur at the same time. Create a merge node only when the conditions for merging are clear.

11.4.7Note

Understanding this section

11.4.7 Step Seven: Generate Paths at Branch Points

Branching is not about writing many stories; it preserves conditional differences that may still change the answer. Distinguish ‘only one can occur’ from ‘they may occur together’, then decide between separate and parallel branches.

Branches may arise from condition values, near-threshold states, actors’ choices, external disturbances, or mechanism uncertainty. State triggering differences, not merely emotional labels ‘optimistic, ordinary, pessimistic’. Branches also need one frozen starting point; otherwise the comparison may silently change initial values.

Mutually exclusive paths cannot both count toward one actual result. An indivisible task choosing either machine A or B within one window has exclusive choices; procurement delay and machine failure may coincide, so forcing them into either/or omits their joint branch.

Co-occurrence also does not mean independence. Branches sharing workers or budgets, or affecting one another’s conditions, need joint states and shared-resource constraints. Separate feasibility cannot establish joint feasibility.

Merge nodes require an explicit contract: which key states, remaining resources, history dependencies, authorities, and future actions are sufficiently identical or equivalent for a bounded task? Equal final stock does not automatically permit merging; failure debt or missed commitments may still affect the next step.

Branch counts are not credibility; ten generated scenarios do not automatically form a frequency distribution. Without probability grounds, retain conditional paths and preserve key branches by impact and distinguishability where necessary. Diagram neatness cannot justify deleting a high-loss branch with substantive possibility. Section 11.9 later addresses path lineage and pruning records.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Generate branches from specific conditional differences that change the task answer.

  2. 2

    Determine exclusivity, co-occurrence, or sequential dependence, constructing joint states when needed.

  3. 3

    Keep starting points, triggers, and resource limits traceable for every branch.

  4. 4

    Merge only when key states meet explicit merger conditions, without default probabilities.

Distinctions to keep clear

Mutually exclusive

Cannot both be true under the same contract.

≠

Parallel and able to co-occur

May happen together, with resources and interactions still checked.

Temporarily equal values

A field agrees at this moment.

≠

Mergeable

Conditions relevant to later tasks are sufficiently aligned.

Fraction of generated branches

How many stories a model listed.

≠

Real-world probability

Needs data and a probability model, not branch counts.

Mathematical construction: two disturbances form four joint conditionsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll four combinations are allowed in the construction; no actual probabilities are given. If conditions persist next hour, both 7s become 8, but flows and intervention responses still differ.

Fictional B0=6 and B1=B0+arrivals−processing after one hour. Arrivals may be 2 or 4, processing 3 or 1. Joint conditions yield (2,3)→5, (2,1)→7, (4,3)→7, and (4,1)→9. Listing only exclusive stories of ‘more arrivals’ and ‘slower processing’ misses their joint 9. The two 7s also arise from different arrival/capacity states; if later conditions persist, current equality at 7 alone does not permit merging.

BoundaryIf only first-hour backlog matters and subsequent mechanisms genuinely do not, the two 7s may share an outcome class while retaining their source branches.

Apollo 13: the return path was not one default actionDocumented case

The report records several propulsion options considered, with the team choosing to use the Lunar Module descent engine as much as possible given propulsion needs and uncertainty about the damaged Service Module. The sole focus here is that option comparison depends on conditions.

SourceNASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15Chapter 4, Part 5, Return to Earth, printed p. 4-48, first half of PDF page 156Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsNot every option’s risks and probabilities are reconstructed; unimplemented options are not recorded as actual paths, and ultimate success does not prove every rejected option would have failed.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleBoth branches reach 7, so they remain equivalent forever.

What it limitsEqual terminal values do not guarantee equal resources, mechanisms, or feasible interventions; merging needs a bounded task.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Omitting joint-occurrence branches misses compound risks.
  • Different mechanisms may yield the same outcome; mechanism tasks do not permit arbitrary merging.
  • Branches need stopping or checking conditions, not infinite elaboration of every imagination.

Scope and open questions

The report explicitly separates considered options from actual choices, illustrating why conditional branches must not enter occurred history.

Why include the jointly occurring outcome 9?

Increased arrivals and reduced capacity may co-occur; forced exclusivity misses joint conditions.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

How may the two 7s be handled if only the first-hour result matters?

They may share a result-value class while retaining distinct source conditions; mechanism identity cannot be declared.

11.4.8Step Eight. Register Signals, Residuals, and Variable Candidates ​

In briefAn unexplained model difference calls for checking, not inventing a new real-world variable’s value. Each path should specify which signals support it and which would change the judgment.

List early and contrary signals for each path. State differences that the current variables cannot explain enter the residuals. A residual can prompt an entry in the ledger of variable candidates, but cannot automatically supply a value in reality.

11.4.8Note

Understanding this section

11.4.8 Step Eight: Register Signals, Residuals, and Variable Candidates

An unexplained model difference calls for checking, not inventing a new real-world variable’s value. Each path should specify which signals support it and which would change the judgment.

Early signals need observation definitions, windows, sources, and associated branches—for example, first observing an actual processing decline, then whether backlog follows the corresponding path. A supporting signal is not absolute proof; check whether competing paths also produce it. A contrary signal is a distinguishable observation weakening the path, without waiting for the endpoint before recognizing failure.

Residuals first depend on model and observation definitions. Observed 8 versus predicted 7 gives residual 1, indicating only this discrepancy. It may reflect unrecorded arrivals, processing-capacity error, mismatched windows, observation error, or omitted mechanisms. Without discriminating material, ‘difference 1’ cannot establish a real variable called collaboration resistance with value 1.

A variable-candidate ledger should record definition, reason for proposal, observation method, supportive and contrary material, competing explanations, and upgrade conditions. It turns questions into testable work, not a new freely adjustable factor for every residual.

Residuals are not automatically random noise. Inference using means, variances, or distributions needs corresponding sampling and error conditions; selective missingness or changed definitions cannot usually be assigned to independent identically distributed error without explanation. Repetition strengthens reasons to investigate, not direct identification of a mechanism.

Prioritize the smallest discriminating observation that changes the current answer or action comparison. More candidates are not inherently better; if a simple recording-definition issue suffices, check it before adding hidden variables to preserve complexity.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Prewrite observable early and contrary signals for every branch, with windows.

  2. 2

    Calculate differences between matched observations and conditional predictions, checking time and measurement first.

  3. 3

    Propose candidates and competing explanations for unexplained parts without assigning actual truth values.

  4. 4

    Design minimal discriminating material, then upgrade, retain, split, or withdraw candidates according to results.

Distinctions to keep clear

Residual

Difference between observation and expectation under the current representation.

≠

A new variable exists

Needs independent definition, measurement, and discriminating support.

Supporting signal

Compatible with a path and potentially strengthens its support.

≠

Unique proof

Requires excluding competing explanations for the same signal.

Contrary signal

Material capable of weakening the current path.

≠

Bad news

Unpleasantness differs from evidentiary responsibility.

Mathematical construction: difference 1 does not identify its causeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe construction assumes an accurate start, no other mechanisms, and provisionally credible observation 8; actual candidates may be more numerous.

Fictional B0=6, recorded arrivals 2 and processing 1 predict B1=7; a new observation records 8, a difference 8−7=1. Explanation A: one arrival was omitted, actual arrivals 3. Explanation B: one processed item was erroneously recorded, actual processing 0. Both give 8. Actual completion records may distinguish them; directly setting ‘team friction=1’ neither excludes these record explanations nor provides a measurable definition.

BoundaryIf completion records also suffer selection or misrecording, a single record cannot again serve as an infallible judge.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleThe model’s unexplained item must result from personality resistance, so resistance is set to 1.

What it limitsThe remaining difference identifies no specific cause; both variable name and value lack independent support.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • No reader or field testing occurred; signal proposals are not claimed validated as effective.
  • A new variable cannot merely be defined to absorb every error exactly.
  • If observation definitions change, update the observation model before rushing to change the world’s mechanism.

Scope and open questions

This section tests the nonimplication from residual to variable through a reproducible construction. Unknown causes in the accident report read are not treated as empirical residuals assignable arbitrary values.

  • Actual residuals require consistently defined observations and frozen predictions. No field data are available here; no error distribution or personality variable is estimated.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Why can difference 1 not directly identify unrecorded arrivals?

  2. 2

    When should contrary signals be registered?

Why can difference 1 not directly identify unrecorded arrivals?

Recording one extra completion, or recording unfinished work as completed, can also produce difference 1, among other unlisted mechanisms; discriminating material is needed.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

When should contrary signals be registered?

Preferably alongside the path before viewing outcomes, preventing any result from becoming post hoc support.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

11.4.9Step Nine. Write Back the Results ​

In briefWhen outcomes arrive, honest comparison matters: what was right, what was wrong, and which simple method was better. Inserting the ending into the original draft is not learning. Preserving that draft and letting new evidence change the next version makes scrutiny possible.

When actual results arrive, append which paths are supported, when results diverged from the projection, whether a simple baseline performed better, how well the projection was calibrated, and which mechanisms or variables should be downgraded, split, given revised boundaries, or retired. Write-back does not overwrite the original run.

11.4.9Note

Understanding this section

11.4.9 Step nine: outcome write-back

When outcomes arrive, honest comparison matters: what was right, what was wrong, and which simple method was better. Inserting the ending into the original draft is not learning. Preserving that draft and letting new evidence change the next version makes scrutiny possible.

Write-back first appends actual outcomes with sources, object-event times, and acquisition times, then matches them to the original run. A news narrative or rerunning a model is not equivalent to actual outcomes. If outcomes have not arrived or definitions do not match, retain unresolved status rather than forcing closure.

Support for a path does not make every mechanism true. Different mechanisms can yield the same outcome, and errors may cancel into apparent success. Examine timing, magnitude, key intermediate signals, and contrary material together. Locate local departures through dependencies; one failure does not make the entire framework useless, nor one success universally effective.

Compare simple baselines for the same target, window, available information, and scoring rule. A queue task might initially use the last observation carried forward. If the complex model performs worse, record it honestly and examine whether complexity adds actual gain. Do not select a baseline afterward merely to lose to the model.

Calibration is a long-term or grouped correspondence property of probability predictions, not one hit. If this run offered conditional branches without probabilities, assess coverage, timing, conditions, and distinguishing power; do not invent probabilities afterward to claim good calibration. Part XII further specifies forecast contracts.

Write-back may downgrade mechanisms, split variables, narrow boundaries, or retire items, rather than merely add explanations. State which new evidence changes which dependency, how the next version handles it, and what remains unknown. Source corrections revise epistemic lineage; changed real conditions require event registration. Do not conflate them.

Creating a next version does not establish improved learning. Claiming it is better requires later independent or appropriately held-out testing. Repeatedly tuning to the same outcome for closer fit demonstrates only adaptation to seen material.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Append actual outcomes and sources to the frozen run, retaining the original prediction and information set.

  2. 2

    Check deviations under original targets, windows, scoring, and baselines; do not change definitions to rescue the model.

  3. 3

    Distinguish path support, mechanism identification, probability calibration, and a single hit.

  4. 4

    Revise the next version along dependencies, stating downgrading or retirement reasons and awaiting new material for testing.

Distinctions to keep clear

An outcome supports a path

The outcome fits that path's conditions.

≠

A uniquely confirmed mechanism

Competing mechanisms may still produce the same outcome.

Fitting a seen outcome

Changing the model using the same material.

≠

Improved generalization in a new version

Requires corresponding new testing, not inference from training fit.

Append-only write-back

Old predictions and new observations both remain.

≠

Overwriting the original run

Destroys the evaluation baseline and may disguise hindsight.

Mathematical construction: a complex model loses to a simple baselineTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll values, measurement status, and scoring are teaching constructions. No actual queue experiment occurred, and one sample does not estimate average performance.

Fictional pending repairs at 08:00 are 6. Beforehand, freeze a model prediction of 4 at 10:00, a carry-forward baseline of 6, and absolute-error scoring. Later, a consistently defined measurement is 7. Model error is |4−7|=3; baseline error |6−7|=1. The baseline wins this occasion. Changed arrivals or processing conditions may be investigated, but rewriting the original prediction to 7 cannot establish perfection.

BoundaryProbability calibration would additionally require prior probabilities and a multi-case evaluation contract. This example concerns point-prediction error only.

Teaching construction: matching final values can conceal an incorrect temporal pathTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThreshold and observations are constructed. Hourly checkpoints are stipulated and do not imply no larger peaks between them.

The original prediction is backlog 5 at 09:00 and 4 at 10:00; observations later give 8 and 4. Endpoint error is 0, but intermediate congestion was missed. If the task's protection condition requires no hourly value above 7, the path judgment failed. Endpoint success cannot conceal an intermediate breach.

BoundaryIf only an endpoint prediction was declared, its hit may remain; it cannot expand into successful prediction of safety throughout.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleThe final value was guessed correctly, so every mechanism, path, and calibration is confirmed.

What it limitsAn endpoint hit does not identify intermediate paths, probability calibration, or a unique mechanism.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleChanging the old prediction to the correct value using new material completes a learning loop.

What it limitsThat overwrites the evaluation reference. Retain the old prediction and test a new version separately.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Without prior probabilities, do not fabricate retrospective calibration performance.
  • Do not record only hits while omitting failures and unresolved cases.
  • One failure may require local revision without automatically proving the whole theory invalid.

Scope and open questions

This section needs a traceable prior run, consistently defined actual outcomes, and a baseline. Available historical accident reports lack the nine-step forecast archive needed here, so retrospective success narratives are not passed off as write-back evaluation. Two examples explicitly show executable evaluation contracts.

  • Actual forecast records, outcomes, and baselines have not been supplied. No field calibration or reader-effect experiment was performed.

  2. 2

    If endpoint 4 is correct but actual 09:00 value 8 exceeds threshold 7, is the whole path successful?

  3. 3

    May scenario branches alone be retrospectively declared well-calibrated probabilities?

With prediction 4, baseline 6, and actual 7, which is better under absolute error?

Model error is 3, baseline error 1; the baseline wins this occasion, without establishing long-term superiority.

If endpoint 4 is correct but actual 09:00 value 8 exceeds threshold 7, is the whole path successful?

No. The endpoint task can succeed while path-protection conditions fail. Register them separately.

May scenario branches alone be retrospectively declared well-calibrated probabilities?

No. Prior probabilities and corresponding evaluation data are required. Conditional coverage is not probability calibration.

11.5Propagation, Delay, and Thresholds ​

In briefA message arriving, being understood, changing a mind, and producing action are different changes. Propagation analysis must specify what changed, through which channel, how long effects take, and within which window they fail.

An account of propagation must at least distinguish the arrival of a signal from an effective change of state. If information is seen but does not change a subsequent transition, record only arrival. If it changes beliefs without prompting action, record the change in experience–meaning state. Register a corresponding structural change only if the signal changes resources, behavior, rules, or relationships.

Propagation FactorQuestion for the RecordPossible Nonlinearity
ChannelWhat carrier conveys the impact from the source to the target?Channel closure, filtering, or substitution
CapacityHow much can be carried per unit of time?Saturation, congestion, and queues
DelayWhen does it arrive, and when does it take effect?Delayed feedback or a mistaken finding of no effect
ThresholdWhat conditions must be reached before the state changes?Abrupt changes, hysteresis, and cascades
LossWhat is lost or changed in propagation?Drift in meaning or dissipation of resources
DirectionIs the impact symmetric?One-way dependence or offsetting effects in the opposite direction
RecoveryHow does the object return to its previous state or move to a new one after a shock?Resilience, cumulative damage, and lock-in

When the same event reaches different circles through different channels, the effects can be opposite. Additional resources may reduce load in one circle but intensify competition in another. A public statement may repair external legitimacy but activate shame or distrust within the circle. A projection should record each channel separately. Net effects must not hide differences in distribution.

11.5Note

Understanding this section

11.5 Propagation, delays, and thresholds

A message arriving, being understood, changing a mind, and producing action are different changes. Propagation analysis must specify what changed, through which channel, how long effects take, and within which window they fail.

The first level is arrival: a system receives a message, presents it, or a person sees it. This supports only the corresponding arrival fact, not changed subsequent transitions. The second is experience–meaning change, such as evidenced belief revision. Retain that change even without action rather than declaring “nothing happened without behavior.” The third concerns changes to resources, behavior, rules, or relations, each registered by material rather than bundled as “effective.”

These levels are not a mandatory linear staircase. Resources can transfer before a person understands, and reading can alter understanding without behavior. Explain cross-channel bridges individually; exposure rates cannot directly become agreement rates or institutional-implementation rates.

The table's first item, channel, asks what carries the process: circuits, logistics, face-to-face exchange, rule implementation, or platform presentation each have objects and interfaces. Closure, filtering, and substitution change who receives what. An email's existence does not establish that its recipient read it; reading does not establish execution authority.

Capacity is measured per unit time and may saturate, queue, or congest. Delay distinguishes arrival from onset: one-second forwarding, one-day understanding, and one-week approval may coexist. No outcome before the predetermined effect window is not immediate proof of ineffectiveness. No response beyond a reliable maximum delay should count as contrary material. If the maximum delay is unknown, invent no deadline.

Thresholds specify conditions for state transitions, potentially with jumps or hysteresis. Loss concerns resource dissipation, information omission, and meaning transformation; the latter two may lack a common percentage measure. Direction reminds us that A affecting B does not imply equally strong B→A influence; opposing effects may also cancel.

Recovery asks how an object returns or enters a new state after a shock. Elastic recovery, cumulative damage, and lock-in are patterns to distinguish, not defaults for all systems. Separate recovery onset, local availability, and complete recovery. Availability of one core service does not instantly clear backlogs and downstream effects.

The same event may have opposite effects on different circles through different channels. The original resource/public-explanation example describes possible mechanisms, not grounds for declaring a group's shame or distrust without actual experiential material. Register by channel and position. Net totals may serve a specified statistical task without hiding burden bearers or protected constraints.

The requirement is responsibility for propagation statements, not complex simulation every time. A receipt or suitable log may suffice to establish document arrival; changed rules require decision, execution, and actual-outcome material. Task evidence requirements cannot be arbitrarily escalated, nor may an easily obtained indicator silently replace the question.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify whether the target change concerns arrival, experience–meaning, or resources/behavior/rules/relations, with its observation definition.

  2. 2

    Check channel, capacity, delay, threshold, loss, direction, and recovery individually. Supply material for applicable items and reasons for inapplicable ones.

  3. 3

    Separate arrival time, possible effect window, and recovery milestones.

  4. 4

    Examine distributional consequences across positions and circles; net values cannot replace every component.

  5. 5

    Distinguish conditional mechanisms from observed changes and revise paths under contrary signals.

Distinctions to keep clear

Signal arrival

Corresponding facts of receipt, presentation, or being seen.

≠

Effective state change

Requires evidence of subsequent state or transition changes.

Meaning change

Evidenced change in belief, interpretation, or experience.

≠

Behavior change

Requires separate material showing action; neither substitutes for the other.

Recovery begins

Some capability becomes available again.

≠

Complete recovery

Relevant interfaces, backlogs, and downstream conditions meet declared standards.

Net effect

A total under a specified aggregation rule.

≠

Distributional structure

Which positions benefit and which bear losses must still be shown independently.

Before the effect window

Temporary absence of outcomes may fit the delay.

≠

Established ineffectiveness

Requires a reasonable predeclared window and adequate detection capability.

Mathematical construction: separate capacity and delayTeaching scenario

AssumptionsArrivals, processing order, constant capacity, and fixed effect delay are teaching assumptions. Processing is lossless and newly arrived messages may be processed in the same minute.

A fictional information-processing queue starts with 4 messages, receives 2 per minute, and processes at most 3. Under Q_next=max(0,Q+2−3), queue lengths are 3,2,1 in the first three minutes and 0 in the fourth. If arrival additionally requires a fixed 2 minutes before downstream state changes, clearing the queue does not mean the last message's effect has occurred. Queue waiting and effect delay are registered separately.

BoundaryUnderstanding or executing actual messages need not follow fixed minute delays; this example estimates no human response speed.

Mathematical construction: hysteresis is not one threshold applied both waysTeaching scenario

Assumptions80 and 70 are teaching thresholds, not equipment safety standards. Initial operation at 75 is stipulated.

A fictional device shuts down at T≥80 and, once stopped, restarts only at T≤70, retaining its prior state between them. For 75→82→76→69, states are running→stopped→still stopped→restarted. Recording only current 76 without prior shutdown misclassifies recovery.

BoundaryOffers no actual device-control advice and does not claim hysteresis in every system.

Teaching construction: net burden reduction cannot hide positional differencesTeaching scenario

AssumptionsValues, comparable units, and causal differences are constructed, not measured in actual groups.

The same fictional resource reallocation reduces group A's weekly waiting by 10 hours but increases group B's by 8. If the task declares the groups' hours additive, net reduction is 2 hours, while B still worsens. If B faces a nonwaivable deadline constraint, net reduction 2 does not automatically make the option acceptable.

BoundaryWhether waiting across people can be added and which weights to use require separate normative explanation. This example authorizes nothing for stakeholders.

The 2017 S3 incident: local and downstream recovery have different timesDocumented case

AWS's review of the February 28, 2017 US-EAST-1 incident records partial-request recovery in the index subsystem beginning at 12:26 PST, relevant read/delete/list APIs operating normally by 13:18, and the separate subsystem required for writes recovering at 13:54. Some dependent services had backlogs requiring additional time. This distinguishes recovery onset, interface availability, and full downstream recovery.

SourceAWS incident reviewSecond main-text paragraph, counting “We’d like…” after the title as the first; sentences beginning “The index subsystem…” and “At this point…”Reading scope: Read

Scope and limitsA primary operator review, without individual customer logs. It cannot imply simultaneous restoration for all users or estimate a general recovery distribution.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleRead receipts reach 100%, so the institution is declared implemented.

What it limitsArrival evidence cannot certify execution or actual write-back.

Teaching counterexampleTemperature falls from 82 to 76, below 80, so operation must have resumed.

What it limitsThe explicit hysteresis construction still requires reaching 70. Historical state changes the current judgment.

Teaching counterexampleThe two groups improve by 2 hours in total, so each group benefits.

What it limitsAggregate conclusions do not imply individual or positional improvement; B's waiting still increases by 8 hours.

What does not follow

  • The same threshold need not be universal. Thresholds, reversal, and hysteresis need object material or explicit constructions.
  • Experiential change may hold without action, but does not establish rule implementation.
  • Zero net effect may hide gains on one side and losses on another; value comparison additionally requires normative premises.
  • No short-term change is not automatically ineffectiveness, but endlessly extending windows cannot protect a model either.
  • A source report's recovery standard applies only to its declared services and operations, not simultaneous recovery for every customer.

Scope and open questions

The same actual outage explicitly records staged recovery and downstream backlogs, directly matching the distinction between delay and recovery.

  • No per-customer recovery or experience records were obtained; platform recovery milestones do not establish every user's state.
